We report for the first time ESLD (end-stage liver disease) as a prognostic factor for survival. The renal function (expressed as serum creatinine) and urinary Na (<5 mEq/l) at the time of diagnosis were found to be associated with survival, suggesting that early treatment might increase survival.

This finding suggests that monitoring kidney function and assessing urinary sodium levels may provide additional information about a patient's prognosis for ESLD.
